view: The line this print turns on is whether the ~100% FY26 growth target survives. H1 revenue was $3.16M, and $2.05M of that was Q2, 74% from one EMEA distributor. That leaves about $7.2M needed in H2 against a Q3 2025 comparison of about $2.0M gross. The company opened Q3 with $1.2M of Brazil and India orders and announced them on 2026-07-13. It press-released even small domestic orders in H1 (Carolina Beach, Galveston, UMBC, Panama). Since July 13 there has been no order or booking release at all. Releases since then cover training certifications, a new director, a VP of training, a new COO, and a WrapShield/Frenel engineering milestone on the morning of the print. That silence is the strongest dated evidence I found: Q3 revenue probably lands near the $1.2M of international orders plus a modest domestic and services base, around $1.5-2.5M. That makes the 100% target arithmetically very hard, and it is likely to be softened, dropped or reframed around bookings. The price, though, has already fallen about 30% since the Q2 print to below the August offering price, so a lot of disbelief is in it. There is no consensus to miss, and promotional framing ('revenue up X% YoY', COO hire, subscriptions, ATF ruling, private security) has produced up-moves at three of five prints. Short interest of about 11.5% with high days-to-cover could amplify any good headline at a thin open. On balance I lean mildly down, because the target probably breaks, but the evidence that the price does not already hold it is weak.
unpriced: Possibly the specific scale of the H2 shortfall against the 100% target. Order announcements stopped after July, but the market has already de-rated the stock by about 30% since August, so I cannot show the gap is unpriced.

recommendation.reason: The evidence points to a weak Q3 against the self-set 100% FY26 target: no order releases since July 13 from a company that releases small orders, and Q2 revenue concentrated in one distributor. But the stock has already fallen about 30% since the last print, there is no consensus, and short interest is about 11.5%, so I cannot show the price fails to hold this. The lean is not strong enough to bet.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: A Q3 revenue figure at or above about $3M, or disclosed Q4 backlog or bookings that keep the 100% target alive, would send this up sharply through the short base.

self_critique: The silence on orders may just reflect a shift in PR focus to training and WrapShield. Distributor orders such as the EMEA one in Q2 were not pre-announced either, so a lumpy Q3 shipment could surprise. The stock has already de-rated about 30%, sits below the raise price and carries about 11.5% short interest with roughly 19 days to cover. A promotional 'revenue up X% YoY' headline at a thin opening print could move it up even if the target is dropped. Three of five prior prints were up.
approach_notes: P3's 'freshest data first' paid: the gap in the company's own press-release flow after July was the most informative trace. P4 cut the other way: I could not show the de-rating fails to hold the weakness, so the lean stayed below the recommendation bar. For microcaps with no consensus and no option chain, the playbook could say more about how to treat the company's own target as the bar.
